ops.title: Use cast(float, x) not float(x) for pandas itertuples Scalar narrowing
ops.body: When narrowing pandas `.itertuples()` row attributes to float, use `typing.cast(float, r.attr)` rather than `float(r.attr)`. Pyright's `float.__new__` signature expects `ConvertibleToFloat` which rejects the `Scalar` union type returned by itertuples. `cast` is a pure type-only no-op at runtime — it does not call `__float__`. Applies to any `.itertuples()` attribute access in pyright-checked code.
ops.why: G3 implementer discovered float() was rejected by pyright on Scalar; cast() is the correct type-only fix

ops.title: Attach review-result to gN-integrate (not just gN-review) for c2 postcondition
ops.body: The engine's `gN-integrate` gate has a `c2` postcondition that checks for a `review-result` artifact with `verdict: APPROVE`. This artifact must be attached to `gN-integrate` directly (via `attach gN-integrate --type review-result --field verdict=APPROVE`), not just to `gN-review`. The pattern: (1) close gN-review normally, (2) start gN-integrate, (3) attach review-result to gN-integrate, (4) call advance gN-integrate.
ops.why: First advance call for g1-integrate failed with 'postconditions unmet [c2]' because review-result was only on g1-review

ops.title: Diff against merge-base when origin/main advances during a run
ops.body: When origin/main advances while a feature branch is in-flight, `git diff origin/main --name-only` will show upstream commits as if they were your changes. Always use `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) HEAD --name-only` to see only your commits. This matters for reconcile (architecture impact) and PR description accuracy.
ops.why: cmdr-T's #546 merged to main while this branch was in-flight; diff origin/main showed decoupled_*.py as if they were my changes
